content.title: WebAgents demo index
content.description: The agents of the WebAgents research prototype: a literature-review agent, a fictional airline's agent, a travel network that delegates between roles within a stated envelope, and a travel planner that asks other publishers' agents for help (Agent Links), with the three agents it can ask. Signed with a development key, for demonstrations only; every entry is metadata, and each package is verified when you open it.

entries.name: Literature Review Agent
entries.description: A constrained coordinator-worker literature review: searches Crossref, screens and reads candidate papers (and PDFs you pick), resolves citations and writes a related-work draft with verified quotes, and lists every paper it found with its screening verdict. With your leave it reads your research profile, keeps its own notes and proposes to remember the review. Its candidate deduplication runs as a WebAssembly module that can only compute.

entries.name: WebAir Travel Agent
entries.description: Talk to WebAir: search flights, ask about fares and rules, get a booking quote and simulate buying it, in one conversation through WebAir's own semantic API, using the travel profile you choose from your memory. Before a simulated purchase your browser asks you, with the quote's facts in front of you. Your browser checks WebAir's fare totals with a WebAssembly module that can only compute. WebAir is a fictional demo airline: nothing is ever booked or charged.

entries.name: Travel Network
entries.description: Plan a trip with a small team: a front man restates your trip and, choosing as it goes, consults a flights, a hotel and a calendar role, each at most once, then answers with the plan. Your browser tells you the envelope before you run it (at most 6 handoffs, 8 model calls, 19 remote calls and 48,000 tokens) and records every handoff with the reason it was allowed. The data comes from the WebAir demo origin's fictional travel services: nothing is booked.

entries.name: Tripwright
entries.description: Plan a trip with help from other publishers' agents: a front man asks WebAir Flights for the flights and Staymere for the hotels, two signed packages from two other publishers, and checks your calendar. Your browser verifies both first, shows each publisher on its own card and lets you deny one; each runs here, on your model. At most 6 handoffs, 10 model calls, 23 remote calls and 92,000 tokens. All data is fictional: nothing is booked.

entries.name: WebAir Flights
entries.description: WebAir's flight search as an agent another agent can ask: it searches WebAir's fictional flights for one date and proposes one among them. Linked from another package it runs in your browser on your model, under what you grant it on its own card. All data is fictional: nothing is booked.

entries.name: Staymere
entries.description: A fictional hotel aggregator's search as an agent another agent can ask: it searches the hotels it lists in a city for a stay and proposes one among them. Linked from another package it runs in your browser on your model, under what you grant it on its own card. All data is fictional: nothing is booked.

entries.name: Hotel Salitubam
entries.description: A fictional small hotel in Reykjavik as an agent another agent can ask or find: it checks the hotel's own availability for a stay and proposes one room offer. All data is fictional: nothing is booked.
